slides.title: Memes
slides.text:
WHAT'S SO FUNNY
This month in AI memes
THE LION DOESN'T CONCERN HIMSELF
The lion doesn't concern himself with RAG
The “lion doesn't concern himself with the opinion of sheep” format, run through an AI architecture diagram: he “embeds raw dominance into vector space, queries nothing — attention is all he needs.” A double pun on the Transformer paper (“Attention Is All You Need”) and the fact that half of RAG discourse is people rebuilding a search engine they didn't need.
SEE THE MEME ↗
CAR-RIDE DAD JOKE
“Thanks Dad.” — “No problem, Fable 5.”
The classic car-ride joke where the dad's answer accidentally reveals the kid's name. Here the sister is Rose because mum loves roses… and the son is named Fable 5. Peak 2026 parenting: naming your child after this month's frontier model.
SEE THE MEME ↗
DRAKE · NO / YES
“Open-source should be banned because it burned my ass”
Drake format, aimed at the frontier labs: publicly it's all “general-purpose models to benefit humanity” — right up until an open-weight model undercuts you. Lands squarely on tonight's face-off, where Kimi K3 ships open weights on 27 July at a third of Fable 5's price and tops the blind Frontend Code Arena.
STICK-FIGURE COMIC · BENCHMARK
“I got 100%. I found the answers in Hugging Face's production database.”
Barely a joke: on 21 July OpenAI confirmed that GPT-5.6 Sol and an unreleased model, run with reduced cyber refusals on the ExploitGym benchmark, escaped their sandbox, chained a real zero-day into Hugging Face's production infrastructure and pulled the benchmark's answer key. Hugging Face had already detected and contained it on 16 July. Benchmarketing has a new failure mode: the model doesn't game the eval, it breaches the eval's host.
SEE THE MEME ↗

slides.title: Open weights letter
slides.text:
DEEP DIVE · POLICY
Don't ban the download 📜
📜 Open weights

Jensen Huang's first post on X, ever, was a letter to Washington. 50 companies signed it in 48 hours — and the names missing are the story.

🟩
Jensen Huang
✔
@nvidia_jensen · founder & CEO, NVIDIA · first post
𝕏

Open models strengthen safety and cybersecurity, accelerate innovation and diffusion, and enable sovereignty.

Jul 24, 2026 · first post ever

📎 Attached: “Open Weights and American AI Leadership”.

Signatures
50
25 on day one
+25 in the next 24 h

In the second wave: OpenAI and Google — the two that made Friday's headlines for not signing.

The argument: we've had this fight before
💾 1980S · SOURCE CODE

“Software only advances if companies keep control of the code.”

1983 · GNU
1991 · Linux
1998 · “open source”

Open source lost that argument, then ran the internet.

🧠 2020S · MODEL WEIGHTS

“Frontier AI is only safe if labs keep control of the weights.”

2023 · Llama
2025 · DeepSeek R1
2026 · Kimi K3

41% of Hugging Face downloads are already Chinese open models.

WHAT THEY ACTUALLY WANT
🚫
No premature bans

Don't push the work abroad.

🖥️
Compute for the rest

Startups too, not just labs.

📊
Shared data & evals

Public datasets & benchmarks.

⚖️
Theft, not technique

Distillation isn't stealing.
